column1: # Colbert-Croissy Cipher (1668-1674) (Tomokiyo's own label "DE=68"), reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo, printed
# as a clean digital table ("Colbert-Croissy Cipher (1668-1674)") in sources/cryptiana/web/louisxiv0.htm,
# image louisxiv_0croissy1668.png (fetched from cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/louisxiv_0croissy1668.png,
# INTAKE-SAVOY, 27 Sept 2026). Per the page's own prose this cipher is used across many Melanges de Colbert
# volumes 149, 158-167, 176bis (October 1668-December 1673, mostly Colbert de Croissy's London despatches to
# Lionne/Seignelay) and is the key named for the undeciphered letter of "Mr l'Evesque de Beziers", Melanges de
# Colbert 155, Madrid, 13 August 1670 -- this letter is an outlier in both sender (Beziers, not Croissy) and
# place (Madrid, not London) for an otherwise London-Paris correspondence key; flagged as a risk for the
# reader, not resolved by this transcription job.
# THREE SEPARATE NUMERAL CODE-SPACES share the same digit range, distinguished only by a diacritic mark
# printed directly over the numeral in the source table: none (bare digit), macron (an overbar over the
# digit), circumflex (a caret/hat over the digit). "sign" is the printed code number; "diacritic" is
# none|macron|circumflex; "value" is the plaintext meaning (a single letter, a syllable, or a whole word/
# name). Decode direction: (sign, diacritic) -> value. Two cells use a non-digit printed sign instead of a
# number: "x" -> a, "θ" (Greek theta) -> e, transcribed as drawn per CRYPT B4 (marks recorded as drawn, not
# folded into a digit guess). Bracketed values like [gi], [bu], [hi], [hu], [quu], [vu], [tu], [pu], [ji] are
# printed in square brackets in the source itself -- kept exactly as printed, not this worker's uncertainty
# marker (distinct from the "grade" column below, which IS this worker's own transcription confidence).
# This is a printed digital table (clean typeset HTML/image, not a hand-drawn manuscript key), read by direct
# inspection of three overlapping upscaled crops (crop_left/crop_mid/crop_right, 2x resize) plus one
# independent blind Sonnet subagent read of the same three crops (general-purpose agent, shown only the crop
# images and a transcription task, no context) as a cross-check, per this job's brief. The two reads AGREED
# on every row with no disagreement to settle, including which numeral ranges carry the macron mark (a first
# unaided glance at the full un-cropped image mistook the 81-105 range for undecorated/bare; both crop-based
# reads independently confirmed the overbar is drawn on 81-105 too, resolving that in favour of macron). All
# rows: grade AB (both reads agreed).
# Three cells are printed with a macron-marked numeral (40, 54, 55) but an EMPTY meaning cell in the source
# table itself -- not a transcription gap, the source prints no value there. Recorded below with value
# "(blank in source)" and grade H (read correctly as blank, not an uncertain read). Sign 55 also exists,
# separately, as a genuine value in the circumflex code-space ("hollandois") -- two different codes sharing
# the bare digit 55, correctly kept as two rows.
# Columns: sign
